fine_trace.note: The AV1 bitstream is parsed from the fuzzer input, providing attacker-controlled frame dimensions, segmentation data, and tile information.

fine_trace.code: tile width/height computed from frame dimensions
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled frame size and tile configuration determine the tile grid dimensions used for reconstruction.

fine_trace.code: loop over tile rows and columns
fine_trace.note: The decoder iterates over the tile grid; an out-of-range tile index can be derived from malformed tile size data.
Superblock row/column indices are computed from tile position and frame dimensions; a mismatch between tile dimensions and frame dimensions can cause out-of-bounds access.

fine_trace.code: parse block mode info and segmentation
fine_trace.note: The block's segmentation ID is read from the bitstream and used to index into the segmentation map array.
The segmentation map is indexed using the superblock coordinates; if the coordinates exceed the allocated map dimensions, this reads out of bounds.
The out-of-bounds read returns an 8-byte value (READ 8) that is used as the segment ID for prediction and reconstruction.

fine_trace.code: use seg_id to index segment feature data
fine_trace.note: The corrupted segment ID is used to index into segment feature arrays, potentially causing further out-of-bounds access and memory corruption.

fine_trace.code: motion compensation / intra prediction using seg_id
fine_trace.note: The segment ID influences prediction mode and reference frame selection, propagating the corrupted value through the reconstruction pipeline.

fine_trace.code: write reconstructed block to frame buffer
fine_trace.note: The reconstructed block is written to the frame buffer; the corrupted segment data can cause the write to use incorrect strides or offsets, leading to heap-buffer-overflow.
